statement: Release DevRelay as a deterministic open-source source/library distribution that can be used end to end from ChatGPT Desktop on Windows to build production-quality software.
objectives: Publish the complete DevRelay source and an installable release tarball through GitHub without publishing to the public npm registry.
Make every declared package export resolve from the packed and installed artifact, including ArchitectureDiscovery module and plug-in manifests.
Adopt Apache-2.0 licensing, DCO contribution governance, public support guidance, and a private vulnerability-reporting path.
Protect main as the default branch and require verified release evidence before promotion.
Run the complete released DevRelay lifecycle and a small end-to-end software dogfood from ChatGPT Desktop on Windows before BusinessAcceptance.
constraints: GitHub source and an installable release tarball are the only V0.10 distribution channels.
The supported end-user host for this release is ChatGPT Desktop on Windows.
The default branch is main and must be protected.
No candidate becomes authoritative without deterministic validation, exact evidence, and Gate progression.
acceptanceCriteria: A clean consumer can install the GitHub-produced tarball and resolve every declared package export.
The release includes Apache-2.0 LICENSE and NOTICE files plus DCO, contribution, conduct, governance, support, and security guidance.
CI and local release verification pass on supported Node versions, with Windows as the release-defining environment.

The complete released DevRelay lifecycle produces requirements, design, contracts or a disposition, work planning, execution, verification, integration, system evidence, and business acceptance for this change.
A separate minimal software project completes the same end-to-end path from ChatGPT Desktop on Windows.
assumptions: The owner has approved Apache-2.0 with DCO, GitHub-only distribution, the security contact, and protected main.
The bounded OpenSpec adapter uses ChatGPT as its host-supplied capability executor and does not claim an upstream OpenSpec CLI invocation.
Public npm publication, a one-click Desktop plug-in, and a hosted backend are outside V0.10.
